meta.credit_data_note: Credit ratios for HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bajaj Finance and Cholamandalam use the supplied extracted series where available. The six additional peer histories and the all-company historical slippage/write-off/credit-cost model are simulated academic estimates; they are not company-reported annual-report data.

events.name: Demonetisation announcement
events.detail: Nationwide cash and payment shock affecting borrowers and lenders. The announcement came after market hours on 8 Nov.

events.name: IL&FS liquidity shock
events.detail: Funding stress and risk aversion spread across NBFCs. Treat this as a sector shock window, not a single-cause day.

events.name: COVID-19 market crash
events.detail: Pandemic-driven market crash and lockdown shock; moratorium/standstill measures later delayed NPA recognition.

events.name: RBI restrictions on HDFC Bank digital launches
events.detail: First trading session after RBI restrictions announced on 2 Dec 2020; operational/supervisory event rather than a credit event.

events.name: Russia–Ukraine war begins / global risk-off shock
events.detail: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022. The Indian equity session saw a sharp risk-off move; event-day comparisons use the supplied adjusted-close equity series and relevant sector index. This event overlaps broader commodity, inflation and monetary-policy news, so it is not a single-cause estimate.

events.name: HDFC Ltd–HDFC Bank merger announced
events.detail: Specific corporate event. Merger became effective 1 Jul 2023 and creates a FY2024 comparability break.

events.name: Bajaj Finance RBI restrictions / consumer-credit risk weights
events.detail: Bajaj eCOM/EMI restriction and a sector-wide RBI risk-weight announcement overlap on the same session; reactions cannot be isolated cleanly.

notes: Academic simulation disclosure: FY2017–FY2026 annual GNPA/NNPA/PCR histories for Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank, Shriram Finance, L&T Finance and Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services are modelled estimates anchored to the available FY2026 snapshots. Historical slippage, write-off and credit-cost series are illustrative modelled estimates. They are suitable for explaining formulas and event-period patterns, not for factual company claims or external audit.

Modelled flow formulas: Slippage ratio = gross fresh NPA additions ÷ average advances/AUM × 100; write-off ratio = write-offs ÷ average advances/AUM × 100; credit cost = impairment/provision charge ÷ average advances/AUM × 100. For simulated observations, the numerator and denominator are model assumptions.

The annual credit-risk series currently contains verified extracted financial data for HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bajaj Finance and Cholamandalam only. The other six selected peers have FY2026 snapshot metrics and ten-year share-price histories, but their full FY2017–FY2026 annual-report credit-risk history has not been extracted into the research pack. Do not imply otherwise.
FY2024 onward HDFC Bank includes HDFC Ltd following merger effective 1 July 2023; balance-sheet scale and portfolio composition are not like-for-like with earlier years.
ICICI net NPA denominator varies in the historical source extraction: FY2017–FY2021 uses customer assets in some disclosures, FY2022 onward net advances. Mark the break; do not splice without caveat.
Chola FY2017 uses IGAAP; later figures use Ind AS. GNPA/NNPA and Stage 3 are distinct metrics; do not treat as interchangeable.
Bajaj asset-quality ratios in the annual workbooks are consolidated; capital adequacy ratio is standalone. Chola and bank data are standalone as specified in source workbooks.
Bank advances and NBFC AUM/business assets are not identical denominators. Keep sector peer analysis separate.
Credit cost is not uniformly populated across all entities; provisions/impairment charges cannot be divided by arbitrary balances and called credit cost.
Price-return/GNPA-change correlation uses a small number of FY observations and is descriptive only. Correlation does not establish causality.

Event-day excess return is company return minus sector-index return on the first tradable event session. It is a simple one-day benchmark-relative measure, not a market-model abnormal return or a causal estimate. Events with overlapping announcements are flagged.

The 2016–2026 equity history is suitable for all selected companies. Use of the 2014–2026 ZIP as the project master price file is discouraged because the Nifty Financial Services Index series is missing from that download.
